speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) how many cases of small fires on expressways or roads have been reported in the last five years; and (b) how many of these fires have been caused by errant motorists or motorcyclists who throw their cigarette butts onto the central dividers or roadside plants and trees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: We encourage the public to report such offences via NEA's website, its mobile app or its hotline.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am a bit surprised to know that there are so many fires annually caused by cigarette butts on roads.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We know that in public places and in our estates, NEA takes a very serious approach to littering.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But it is probably a little bit difficult when motorists are on the go and they litter as they drive or ride.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: So, what other forms of action or enforcement can be taken against them?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And to what extent are the fines imposed?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there demerit points or compulsory community action, for instance, imposed on them once they are caught?
